prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get `token_expiry_time` recomputed, so `is_token_valid()` treats an actually-expired token as valid and skips proactive refresh. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` when `expires_in` is present on loaded tokens, and adds an `expired_tokens` fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time...') and instead patches the symptom by inserting a refresh-token attempt inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler before falling back to full re-authorization. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get `token_expiry_time` recomputed, so `is_token_valid()` treats an actually-expired token as valid and skips proactive refresh. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` when `expires_in` is present on loaded tokens, and adds an `expired_tokens` fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time...') and instead patches the symptom by inserting a refresh-token attempt inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler before falling back to full re-authorization. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the root cause in `_initialize()` with a 4-line change plus a dedicated `expired_tokens` test fixture, versus #2875's larger addition of a new branch inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401-handling path that treats the symptom (its own comment cites the exact bug #1784 fixes as the reason the workaround is needed). prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection attempts are exhausted (MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS), the transport previously just logged and returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request hanging forever with no error ever delivered. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection attempts are exhausted (MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS), the transport previously just logged and returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request hanging forever with no error ever delivered. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 patches _handle_reconnection directly at the exact failure site: it builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the specific pending request's id (via ctx.session_message.message.id) and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected in-flight call resolves with an error while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098's _unwrap_exception helper implies the fix instead raises a StreamableHTTPError that gets wrapped in an anyio ExceptionGroup and must be unwrapped at the boundary — a broader-blast-radius approach (propagating out through the task group) that isn't scoped to the single affected request the way #2395's targeted JSON-RPC error response is.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both change the buffer size used when creating the stdio transport's write_stream memory-object stream, which defaults to 0 (a synchronous rendezvous channel) and causes senders to block until a receiver is ready to consume — surfacing as a handler being unable to queue a final response while stdout_writer is still busy flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both change the buffer size used when creating the stdio transport's write_stream memory-object stream, which defaults to 0 (a synchronous rendezvous channel) and causes senders to block until a receiver is ready to consume — surfacing as a handler being unable to queue a final response while stdout_writer is still busy flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2654 fixes the default behavior directly (write_stream buffer 0→1) so every caller benefits without opt-in, and ships a dedicated regression test (a BlockingStdout harness that simulates a slow stdout write racing a queued response) proving the exact deadlock scenario is resolved. PR #2215 only adds optional buffer-size parameters that default to 0, so it doesn't change out-of-the-box behavior and requires callers to know to pass a size — it doesn't fix the reported blocking by itself. #2215's diff is also built against an older version of stdio.py (calls anyio.create_memory_object_stream(0) directly) while #2654 is built on the current create_context_streams[...](0) helper introduced by a later refactor, so #2215 is stale and will need a rebase / hit merge conflicts on the same lines #2654 already touches.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Its diff (88 lines added) goes further than #3012 (45 lines shown for the splitter): it adds _split_www_authenticate_segments plus a dedicated _extract_bearer_auth_params that explicitly isolates the Bearer-scheme segment before pulling params, so a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer error=...') won't leak params from a non-Bearer scheme. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only tokenizes params after the first space with no scheme-boundary handling visible in the diff, so it does not appear to address multi-scheme headers, only comma-splitting within a single challenge.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py over-eagerly JSON-decodes string input for any field annotation other than exactly `str`, which corrupts values for str-containing unions (e.g. `str | None`) whenever the incoming string happens to look like valid JSON (e.g. the literal text "null", "true", or a number) — silently turning it into None/bool/int instead of keeping the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py over-eagerly JSON-decodes string input for any field annotation other than exactly `str`, which corrupts values for str-containing unions (e.g. `str | None`) whenever the incoming string happens to look like valid JSON (e.g. the literal text "null", "true", or a number) — silently turning it into None/bool/int instead of keeping the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same line in pre_parse_json (`field_info.annotation is not str` check) with a helper that decides when to skip JSON pre-parsing. #3056's _is_optional_str narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and leaves pre-parsing behavior unchanged for other unions like `str | list[str]` or `str | int`, where JSON decoding a numeric/array-looking string is still required to produce the non-str member. It also unwraps `Annotated[...]` via _unwrap_annotated before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` params are handled correctly. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead skips pre-parsing for *any* union composed solely of str/int/float/bool/None, which would also silently disable pre-parsing for annotations like `str | int`, changing existing behavior for cases outside the reported bug, and it doesn't unwrap Annotated members before the simple-type membership check, so Annotated-wrapped union members fall through to the pre-parse path unnecessarily.

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same line in pre_parse_json (`field_info.annotation is not str` check) with a helper that decides when to skip JSON pre-parsing. #3056's _is_optional_str narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and leaves pre-parsing behavior unchanged for other unions like `str | list[str]` or `str | int`, where JSON decoding a numeric/array-looking string is still required to produce the non-str member. It also unwraps `Annotated[...]` via _unwrap_annotated before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` params are handled correctly. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead skips pre-parsing for *any* union composed solely of str/int/float/bool/None, which would also silently disable pre-parsing for annotations like `str | int`, changing existing behavior for cases outside the reported bug, and it doesn't unwrap Annotated members before the simple-type membership check, so Annotated-wrapped union members fall through to the pre-parse path unnecessarily.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 patches _handle_reconnection directly at the exact failure site: it builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the specific pending request's id (via ctx.session_message.message.id) and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected in-flight call resolves with an error while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098's _unwrap_exception helper implies the fix instead raises a StreamableHTTPError that gets wrapped in an anyio ExceptionGroup and must be unwrapped at the boundary — a broader-blast-radius approach (propagating out through the task group) that isn't scoped to the single affected request the way #2395's targeted JSON-RPC error response is.

members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get `token_expiry_time` recomputed, so `is_token_valid()` treats an actually-expired token as valid and skips proactive refresh. #1784 fixes this at the source in `_initialize()` by calling `update_token_expiry()` when `expires_in` is present on loaded tokens, and adds an `expired_tokens` fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time...') and instead patches the symptom by inserting a refresh-token attempt inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler before falling back to full re-authorization. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same line in pre_parse_json (`field_info.annotation is not str` check) with a helper that decides when to skip JSON pre-parsing. #3056's _is_optional_str narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and leaves pre-parsing behavior unchanged for other unions like `str | list[str]` or `str | int`, where JSON decoding a numeric/array-looking string is still required to produce the non-str member. It also unwraps `Annotated[...]` via _unwrap_annotated before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` params are handled correctly. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead skips pre-parsing for *any* union composed solely of str/int/float/bool/None, which would also silently disable pre-parsing for annotations like `str | int`, changing existing behavior for cases outside the reported bug, and it doesn't unwrap Annotated members before the simple-type membership check, so Annotated-wrapped union members fall through to the pre-parse path unnecessarily.

clusters.pick_reason: Its diff (88 lines added) goes further than #3012 (45 lines shown for the splitter): it adds _split_www_authenticate_segments plus a dedicated _extract_bearer_auth_params that explicitly isolates the Bearer-scheme segment before pulling params, so a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer error=...') won't leak params from a non-Bearer scheme. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only tokenizes params after the first space with no scheme-boundary handling visible in the diff, so it does not appear to address multi-scheme headers, only comma-splitting within a single challenge.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive/substring matching to pull out auth-param values, which could incorrectly match across parameter names or across multiple auth-scheme challenges in the same header. Both independently implement a nearly identical character-by-character tokenizer that splits the header on top-level commas while tracking quoted-string state and backslash escapes.
